task.title: Commit the MCP transport and persistence regressions the structural output review required
task.description: Two independent reviews asked for boundary regressions that were only ever demonstrated by throwaway probes, so the closures are pinned by nothing a future change would trip over. Add them as committed tests at the two public boundaries. At the MCP transport (src/mcp/structural-redaction.test.ts): a tool result whose enumerable JSON property name carries a recognized credential must come back as an error with the constant withheld text and a redaction state of format-unsafe with the fixed property-name reason, and the credential must appear nowhere in the transported payload or its metadata; a declared output schema using a local reference together with a supported validation sibling must be refused with the fixed reference-sibling reason; an entity-encoded image source and a multi-candidate srcset must be treated as auto-fetch while an ordinary public link in the same payload is untouched. At persistence (src/security/persistence-sinks.test.ts): serialized JSON with a duplicate member whose overwritten value held a credential must never be materialized with the original bytes, in the shapes the recheck enumerated, namely the JSON-escaped duplicate, its fully escaped variant, and duplicates whose surviving value is an empty string, null or false; the metric string beside a long digit run must stay allowed and redacted. Read the probes named in the context refs to learn the exact shapes rather than inventing your own, then express them as ordinary tests with synthetic values. Verify each new test fails against the pre-fix behavior in a scratch copy, or explain precisely why a given case cannot be inverted without editing production code. Write T32-implementation.md and T32-result.json.

acceptance_criteria: AC2 (AFC-02): synthetic secret is absent from JSON, text resource and error; safe JSON passes its schema; a numeric required field carrying a secret returns format-unsafe rather than an invalid string.
AC5 (AFC-15): a mixed corpus of safe IDs and real secrets allows no field-name bypass; a URL secret is masked; a public Markdown link is not treated as a network send.

Every closure the two reviews demanded is pinned by a committed test at the boundary where the defect was reachable, not only at the pure validator; the full focused security and MCP selection stays green.
constraints: Root /Users/Goodea/goodea/keryx. Read .metaproject/index.md first, then .metaproject/skills/gdskills/quality/tests-creator/SKILL.md. Code search only via bun src/cli.ts ctx rg; commands via bun src/cli.ts ctx run; the global keryx binary is stale, use bun src/cli.ts.

Ownership: ONLY src/mcp/structural-redaction.test.ts and src/security/persistence-sinks.test.ts. No production changes at all, and no changes to any other test file. If a test cannot be written without a production change, say so precisely instead of making one.

Another worker owns src/security/guard.ts, src/security/config.ts and the gate region of src/security/service.ts right now, and a third owns src/security/service.memo.test.ts. Do not touch them, and do not depend on gate behavior that is currently being repaired.
Synthetic credentials only; never embed a real secret, and never assert the raw credential value in a way that writes it into an artifact.
No git state changes, no network, no model calls, no bun test without file arguments, no dependency changes, no edits to flow.json or acceptance-criteria.md.
Return a subagent-result JSON at the artifact_path and reply with STATUS: line first.
